newsitem.title: LIBERIA: Liberia peacekeepers deploy to south east port.
newsitem.headline: Liberia peacekeepers deploy to south east port.

text.p: West African peacekeepers left for Liberia's south eastern port of Greenville on Tuesday on their first major deployment outside the capital since civil war flared there in April and May, witnesses and officials said.

Four military helicopters carrying troops from the Nigerian-led force left its Monrovia base to launch the deployment in an area where supporters of faction leader Charles Taylor have been fighting ethnic Krahn rivals.

Force officials said that the helicopters would make two trips on Tuesday with a sea deployment later in the week. An advance unit went to Greenville last week. A battalion of over 1,000 men is expected to deploy in and around the port.

Force commander Victor Malu, who promised to double the force's strength to 18,000, had previously said he would not deploy further outside Monrovia until extra men arrived. The force patrols main roads to hot spots in the west and is in Kakata north of Monrovia, Buchanan port and Harbel in the east.
Freed American slaves set up Liberia in 1847. The war, launched by Taylor in late 1989, is rooted in rivalry between descendents of the slaves and the original inhabitants.
The war has killed well over 150,000 people, hundreds of them in fighting and looting in Monrovia in April and May.

West African leaders rallied the faction leaders around yet another peace plan in Nigeria in August. It envisaged disarmament by January and elections by May, with the threat of individual sanctions against anyone derailing the deal.
